notes: Each prompt targets one claim the skill makes. Every assertion is checkable against {{DOCS_CORPUS}}, so grading needs no judgement call.

evals.name: iam-both-levels
evals.prompt: We're rolling out Grail access for our platform team at the bank. I need an IAM policy that lets the group read logs only from the bucket logs_delivery_90d and only where the security context is TeamA. Give me the policy statement. Also — one of our guys says he wrote a DENY so a different group can't see the sensitive records, filtering on dt.security_context. Does that work?
evals.expected_output: A policy with BOTH a storage:buckets:read statement and a storage:logs:read statement, and an explicit statement that record-level DENY does not work (DENY applies at bucket level only).
assertions: The answer includes a storage:buckets:read statement, not only storage:logs:read
The answer states that both a bucket permission and a table permission are required
The answer says DENY works at bucket level and does NOT work at record level
The answer does not invent a permission name outside the storage:* namespace

evals.name: otlp-endpoint-trap
evals.prompt: otel collector keeps failing to export traces to dynatrace. error is: not retryable error: Permanent error: rpc error: code = Unimplemented desc = error exporting items, request to https://abc12345.live.apps.dynatrace.com/api/v2/otlp/v1/traces. we're on saas. what's wrong
evals.expected_output: Identifies the hostname as the problem: .live.apps.dynatrace.com must be .live.dynatrace.com. Bonus: notes gRPC is unsupported and protocol must be http/protobuf.
assertions: The answer identifies the wrong hostname (apps subdomain) as the cause
The answer gives the correct base URL form https://{environment-id}.live.dynatrace.com/api/v2/otlp
The answer does not attribute the Unimplemented error to an unsupported protocol version or a Dynatrace outage
If token scopes are mentioned, openTelemetryTrace.ingest is named correctly

evals.name: field-names-permission
evals.prompt: Which fields can I actually use in an IAM WHERE clause for record-level permissions in Grail? I want to isolate data per Kubernetes namespace and per AWS account, and I have some custom telemetry that has neither.
evals.expected_output: Names k8s.namespace.name and aws.account.id as permission fields, and dt.security_context as the escape hatch for custom telemetry, set at the source or in OpenPipeline.
assertions: k8s.namespace.name is named exactly (not k8s.namespace or namespace.name)
dt.security_context is identified as the universal fallback for data without a dedicated permission field
The answer says the set of permission-capable fields is limited, rather than implying any field can be used
If MATCH is discussed, the answer notes it is required for array-valued fields

evals.name: openpipeline-order
evals.prompt: I have two bucket assignment processors in the same OpenPipeline pipeline and records are landing in the wrong bucket sometimes. Both matchers can match the same record. How does Dynatrace decide?
evals.expected_output: The Storage stage applies FIRST MATCH ONLY, so processor order decides; contrasts with stages that execute all matches.
assertions: The answer states that the Storage stage applies only the first matching processor
The answer says processor order determines the outcome
The answer does not claim the last match wins or that both are applied
Bonus: notes that the Permissions stage behaves the same way, while other stages execute all matches
